scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You press a button on the remote, and the TV across the room obeys instantly. But there's no wire. How?

scenes.name: ir
scenes.text: Most remotes use infrared light, a kind of light just beyond red, that our eyes can't see.

scenes.name: led
scenes.text: At the front is a small infrared LED. Pressing a button makes it blink very fast.

scenes.name: code
scenes.text: The pattern of blinks is a code. Each button sends its own pattern of ones and zeros.

scenes.name: carrier
scenes.text: The blinks are switched on and off around thirty eight thousand times a second, so the TV can ignore sunlight and lamps.

scenes.name: receiver
scenes.text: A sensor on the TV catches the pattern, decodes it, and does the action, like volume up.

scenes.name: camera
scenes.text: Point a remote at a phone camera and press a button. Many cameras show the hidden light as a flicker.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Blink a code, catch it, decode it. Follow for more on how things really work.
